answer: An agent marketplace analyzing quartz samples can pay per unique job, never per identity. Clients sign job IDs; an atomic ledger releases each job's escrow only once, after its result passes verification. A ripple of cloned agents cannot multiply payouts for the same work, making duplicate claims no haven for profit. This removes a reward for extra keys, not the keys themselves: weak verification, colluding clients, or monopolized job assignment can still undermine it.
